$comment: The differences the migration is allowed to make, each with the reason it is a
rendering change and not a copy change. The value on every entry is the string
the built page printed or stopped printing, byte for byte, which is why this file
holds some of the site's own em dashes and arrows: it quotes frozen copy exactly
rather than paraphrasing it, because an expectation that does not match is a rule
that fires on nothing.
A route of "*" covers the same difference on every route, and is used only where
that is true: the chrome is on every page, so a chrome change is one decision
rather than twenty-nine. Everything scoped to a subset of routes is written per
route, so a reader can see exactly which pages a difference is on.
The entries group into twenty-eight decisions, and the reason on each entry in a
group is the same sentence with the same argument. The groups are: the chrome’s
product switcher, and the retired footer’s product directory and its five one-line
descriptions; the two pages whose own title band stopped being a header element;
the footer’s heading levels; the documentation rail’s section labels and page
links; the contents rail’s unlabelled anchors becoming labelled ones; the
pager’s arrows becoming words; the eight off-the-shelf product names the stack
grid cannot print; the hero drawing’s twelve node names and six relation verbs;
the instrument panel’s mode and pack annotation; the hero’s eyebrow as one string;
and the not-found page’s code as its heading.
One catch here is worth recording. While the migration was being written, this
tool reported one string changed on the landing that nothing in the plan accounted
for, and it turned out to be an edit made while retyping a paragraph of the
landing’s own copy. The content digest could not see it, because the sentence
does not live in content/, and no other gate in this repository could have seen it
either. So this tool is the reason that frozen string is byte-identical, and that
is the argument for having cut the ledger before the first edit rather than after
it.
